claim: World-model action predictions suffer from Goal-Induced Dynamics Hallucination (GIDH): task instructions causally contaminate deterministic forward environment rollouts independently of physical transition dynamics, inducing planner failure via goal-biased state estimation rather than standard policy misgeneralization.
overlap: High overlap with standard cross-attention goal leakage in conditional diffusion/autoregressive models and known confounding in goal-conditioned world models (e.g., representation collapse in reward-free vs. goal-conditioned dynamics models). Architectural causal edge ablation confirms cross-attention cross-talk, not an fundamentally distinct adversarial vulnerability.
experiment: Task-Level Planning Evaluation with Injected Goal Distractors in Test-Time Search: In a 20-task LIBERO subset using Model-Predictive Control (MPC/TTT trajectory optimization evaluated over 50 seeds), optimize candidate action sequences using the world model's imagined future rewards. Compare Task Success Rate across three conditions using the exact same underlying environment state: (1) True Goal conditioning, (2) Orthogonal Distractor Goal conditioning fed only to the dynamics world model (while keeping the reward/critic conditioned on True Goal), and (3) Distractor Goal with the 9 goal-to-prediction attention edges ablated (dynamics-isolated).
falsifier: If Task Success Rate under the Distractor Goal does not drop statistically significantly compared to True Goal (p > 0.05 via paired bootstrap), or if the edge-ablated dynamics condition achieves lower task success than the leaking distractor condition, the visual token shift (RMSE 0.25-0.31) is task-inconsequential noise rather than an exploitable security/planning vulnerability.
decision: Reject current framing. A 7.0-7.5 score requires establishing actual planning disruption and safety compromise, not just non-zero perceptual representation shifts (RMSE 0.3) from cross-attention edges that were designed to carry task conditioning.
